title: Error Handling: Try, Catch, Throw
description: Learn BPL's exception handling system. Throw errors, catch them by type, and build robust error recovery.

sections.title: Why Exception Handling?
Exception Syntax Comparison
sections.explanation: BPL's try/catch is similar to C++ and Java, but you can throw any type, not just Exception subclasses.

sections.title: Basic Try-Catch
sections.expectedOutput:
10 / 2 = 5
Trying 10 / 0...

lineExplanations.23: try block contains code that might throw.
lineExplanations.26: catch (e: Type) catches errors of that specific type.

sections.title: Error Handling Best Practices
sections.content:
✅ **Create specific error types** - Don't just throw strings

✅ **Include useful info** - Error type, message, context

✅ **Handle at the right level** - Catch where you can recover

✅ **Use defer for cleanup** - Ensures resources are released

✅ **Don't catch and ignore** - At least log the error

❌ **Don't use exceptions for control flow** - They're for errors

❌ **Don't throw in destructors** - Can cause issues

sections.title: Practice: Safe Array Access
sections.instructions:
Create an `IndexOutOfBoundsError` struct with fields: `index: int`, `size: int`.
Write `safeGet(arr: *int, size: int, index: int) ret int` that:
- Returns the element if index is valid
- Throws IndexOutOfBoundsError if index is invalid

Test with array [10, 20, 30, 40, 50] accessing indices 2 and 10.
sections.hint: Check if index < 0 || index >= size before accessing.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
sections.content:
✅ **throw** raises an exception of any type

✅ **try { }** contains code that might throw

✅ **catch (e: Type)** handles specific error types

✅ **catch { }** catches any unhandled exception

✅ Exceptions **propagate up** the call stack

✅ **defer** ensures cleanup even when exceptions occur

✅ Create **custom error types** with descriptive fields

questions.question: What happens if an exception isn't caught?
questions.explanation: Uncaught exceptions cause the program to terminate with an error.

questions.question: What does 'defer' do?
questions.explanation: defer schedules code to run when the current scope exits, even if an exception is thrown.

questions.question: When is catch { } executed?
questions.explanation: catch { } runs when an exception doesn't match any specific catch block.
